direction: Evolve the `score_ruin_nodes` removal-priority hook away from the pure Worst-Cost-removal control toward a stagnation-adaptive hybrid: node score = normalized removal_savings (detour cost saved / route distance) + a capacity-pressure term (demand / capacity times how full the node's route is) + a Shaw-relatedness term (average distance to the node's own route neighbours, i.e. how cheaply the node can be reinserted elsewhere), with the relatedness/mixing weight ramping up with stagnation_ratio and iter_frac so the LNS shifts from intensifying worst-cost destroy early to diversifying relatedness destroy when no improvement is found.

operations.mechanism: Archive is empty (no prior solvers), so the first round should establish a strong, clearly-motivated hook design rather than a random one. KB entry method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 gives the exact template semantics (evolved score_ruin_nodes + deterministic Regret-2 reinsertion + perturbed-route intra_2opt + Record-to-Record acceptance) and the reference control value (Worst-Cost removal = 23.3474 at 500 ms), so worst-cost is the concrete baseline to beat. method-cvrp-lns-shaw-regret documents that pairing worst/related destroy operators with Regret-k repair is the standard way to get complementary removal behaviour; a stagnation-driven mix captures both regimes in a single deterministic hook, which matters under the tight 2000 ms budget where a fixed operator is a single point of failure. Safest option: no postprocess (the only allowed mode), no native-only features, hook stays a pure deterministic NumPy scoring function of the provided arguments.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 2000 ms, a removal-priority score that mixes normalized removal savings with a route-capacity-pressure term and a Shaw-relatedness reinsertability term, with the relatedness weight increasing in stagnation_ratio and iter_frac, will beat the frozen L3-ctrl Worst-Cost removal skeleton (baseline 23.3474 on the M3 blind suite) by escaping local optima repeatedly; the capacity-pressure term specifically helps the heterogeneous-demand instances where worst-cost removal repeatedly destroys cheap-but-large nodes that cannot be reinserted feasibly, so effective improvement should be largest in the high-demand-variance regime.
